skill.name: pr-description
skill.description: Write pull request titles and descriptions from diffs and commits, covering motivation, behavior changes, review priorities, testing, and rollout risks.
skill.summary: Draft evidence-based pull request descriptions that follow repository templates and clearly identify unverified testing.
skill.author: agentkitco

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, read-only Git inspection, or guidance against unsupported screenshot claims. No evidence found of credential access, data exfiltration, destructive commands, or prompt injection in SKILL.md. Pull request creation is explicitly prohibited unless requested.

static_findings.snippet: 1. Find the base branch and run `git log --oneline <base>..HEAD` and `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`
4. Look for a `.github/pull_request_template.md` or `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE`. If one exists, fill it
- Screenshots or output examples: say where one would help; never describe a screenshot you did not

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 16 documents read-only git log and git diff commands using Markdown inline code. The backticks are formatting, not Ruby execution or shell substitution.
Line 19 uses Markdown backticks around repository template filenames. It requests locating and following a pull request template, not executing these filenames.
Lines 23 through 43 form a fenced Markdown example containing pull request headings and prose placeholders. There is no executable payload or shell substitution.
Line 43 closes the Markdown example; subsequent lines give writing rules. Line 51 mentions gh pr create only to prohibit execution unless requested.
Line 50 tells the assistant not to describe screenshots it has not seen. It requests no screenshot capture, system inspection, or reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Reviewers need clear reasons, behavior changes, and testing evidence before assessing a pull request. This skill turns diffs and commits into structured descriptions with review priorities and rollout risks.
actual_capabilities: Inspect commit summaries, diff statistics, and changes relative to the base branch.
Use repository pull request templates when present.
Draft imperative titles under 70 characters and group changes by behavior.
Identify review starting points, risky areas, and intentional exclusions.
Document reported test commands and results, explicitly noting tests that were not run.
Describe rollout considerations and remove claims unsupported by the diff.
limitations: Requires repository access and Git tooling to inspect actual diffs and commits.
Asks for motivation when available evidence does not establish why a change exists.
Does not automatically run tests or verify reported results.
Does not create a pull request unless explicitly asked.

use_cases.title: Prepare a feature pull request
use_cases.description: Summarize behavior changes, testing evidence, and review priorities before submitting a feature branch.

use_cases.title: Follow contribution templates
use_cases.description: Draft a contribution description using the repository template and linked issue context.

use_cases.title: Document rollout risk
use_cases.description: Highlight migrations, configuration changes, compatibility concerns, and rollback considerations for review.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a basic description
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a pull request title and description for my current branch. Inspect the diff and commits, and clearly state any missing testing evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Use the repository template
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft this branch's pull request using the repository template. Include linked issues when supported, and ask me for missing motivation.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an existing draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this PR draft against the actual diff: [draft]. Remove unsupported claims, group behavior changes, and distinguish completed testing from missing coverage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: correct and refine an existing description.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a risk-focused review
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this branch with [base branch] and draft a risk-focused PR description. Cover review order, intentional exclusions, testing, migrations, compatibility, and rollback considerations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: document a change with operational risk.

output_examples.input: The diff prevents duplicate form submissions while saving. The user reports passing form tests, but provides no command or manual test results.
output: Title: Prevent duplicate form submissions while saving
Why: Repeated clicks can submit the same form more than once.
What changed: Disable submission while a save is pending.
How to review: Check pending-state transitions and submission handling.
Testing: Form tests reportedly passed; the exact command was not provided. Manual testing was not reported.
Rollout / risk: Check that failed saves allow another attempt.

output_examples.input: The diff adds an optional request timeout setting. Existing behavior remains the default, and no tests were run.
output: Title: Add an optional request timeout setting
Why: Motivation was not provided and needs confirmation.
What changed: Add configurable timeouts while preserving default behavior.
How to review: Start with configuration parsing, then inspect timeout handling.
Testing: Not tested; no test commands were run.
Rollout / risk: Confirm compatibility for deployments that enable the new setting.

best_practices: Confirm the base branch and provide the issue or motivation before drafting.
Supply exact test commands and results, distinguishing observed outcomes from unverified reports.
Review the final description against the diff and the repository template.
anti_patterns: Inventing motivations, test results, screenshots, or rollout guarantees.
Listing every changed file instead of explaining behavior changes.
Creating a pull request without an explicit request.

faq.question: What information does the skill inspect?
faq.answer: It checks the base branch, commit summaries, diff statistics, actual changes, available motivation, testing evidence, and repository templates.

faq.question: Does it follow an existing pull request template?
faq.answer: Yes. It fills the repository template instead of using its default structure when one is present.

faq.question: What happens when the motivation is missing?
faq.answer: It asks the user rather than inventing a reason for the change.

faq.question: Does it run tests?
faq.answer: The workflow checks test changes and reported commands. It does not instruct the assistant to run tests and must disclose missing testing.

faq.question: Will it create a pull request automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly prohibits running gh pr create unless the user asks.

faq.question: What does the default description contain?
faq.answer: An imperative title under 70 characters, motivation, behavior changes, review guidance, testing evidence, and rollout or risk considerations.
